fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every GCLK register to its power-reset state, except generic clocks and their generators whose CLKCTRL.WRTLOCK reads 1; a 0 does nothing. The reset takes time because of synchronization; CTRL.SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both go to 0 when it is done.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY

registers.name: CLKCTRL
registers.title: Generic Clock Control
notes: Configures the generic clock named in CLKCTRL.ID. Write it as one 16-bit access holding the settings and the ID; to read one clock's settings, first write its ID to CLKCTRL.ID with an 8-bit access, then read the register.
A power reset resets CLKCTRL for every ID, the RTC's included. A user reset resets it only for IDs other than the RTC whose WRTLOCK is 0.

After a power reset: WDT has GEN 0x02, and CLKEN and WRTLOCK each follow the WDT Enable and WDT Always-On bits of the NVM User Row (1 if written to one, 0 if to zero); RTC and all others reset to 0x00 in all three fields.

fields.name: WRTLOCK
fields.text: Writing it locks against further writes the generic clock named by CLKCTRL.ID, the generator named by CLKCTRL.GEN and that generator's division factor; only a power reset unlocks them. Generator 0 can never be locked.

values.text: Generic clock, its generator and division factor unlocked.
Generic clock, its generator and division factor locked.

fields.name: CLKEN
fields.text: Turns the generic clock on or off.

fields.name: GEN
fields.text: Generator feeding this generic clock: 0x0 GCLK0, 0x1 GCLK1, 0x2 GCLK2, 0x3 GCLK3, 0x4 GCLK4, 0x5 GCLK5 (generic clock generators 0 to 5); 0x6-0xF reserved.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Picks which generic clock this CLKCTRL access configures. A power reset resets CLKCTRL for every ID, RTC included; a user reset resets it for an ID other than RTC whose WRTLOCK is 0. After a power reset GEN, CLKEN and WRTLOCK read 0 for every ID except WDT, whose GEN is 0x02 and whose CLKEN and WRTLOCK are 1 when the NVM User Row WDT Enable and WDT Always-On bits are 1, 0 when they are 0. After a user reset: RTC's GEN and CLKEN go to 0 only if WRTLOCK and CLKEN are both 0, otherwise unchanged, and its WRTLOCK is unchanged; WDT's GEN goes to 0x02 and its CLKEN follows the User Row WDT Enable bit if WRTLOCK is 0, otherwise both unchanged, and its WRTLOCK is unchanged; for other IDs GEN and CLKEN go to 0 if WRTLOCK is 0, otherwise unchanged.

registers.name: GENCTRL
registers.title: Generic Clock Generator Control
notes: Configures the generator named in GENCTRL.ID. Write it as one 32-bit access holding the settings and the ID; to read one generator's settings, first write its ID to GENCTRL.ID with an 8-bit access, then read the register.

A power reset resets GENCTRL for every ID, the RTC's generator included. A user reset returns generator 0 to its power-reset value, and every other generator too unless it is a source of the RTC clock or of a locked generic clock; such a generator keeps its value.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Keeps the generator running in standby when it is set to drive its GCLK_IO pin. With GENCTRL.OE at 0 it has no effect, and the generator runs only when a peripheral asks for its clock.

values.text: Generator stops in standby; GCLK_IO sits at the level GENCTRL.OOV sets.
Generator keeps running in standby and drives its GCLK_IO pin.

fields.name: DIVSEL
fields.text: Chooses how the generator divides its clock source. For an undivided source, DIVSEL must be 0 and the generator's GENDIV.DIV must be 0 or 1.

values.text: Output is the source divided by GENDIV.DIV.
Output is the source divided by 2^(GENDIV.DIV+1).

fields.name: OE
fields.text: Sends the generated clock out on GCLK_IO, when GCLK_IO is not chosen as a source in GENCLK.SRC.

values.text: Generator sent out on its GCLK_IO, unless that GCLK_IO is chosen as a source in GENCLK.SRC.

fields.name: OOV
fields.text: Level driven on the GCLK_IO pin whenever that pin is not picked as a source in GENCLK.SRC.

values.text: GCLK_IO is 0 while the generator is off or OE is 0.
GCLK_IO is 1 while the generator is off or OE is 0.

fields.name: IDC
fields.text: Evens out the generator's duty cycle for odd division factors.

values.text: Duty cycle not 50/50 with odd division factors.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: 1 while registers are being synchronized between clock domains; goes to 0 when that finishes.

fields.name: CLEAR
fields.text: Write 0xA5 (KEY) to clear the watchdog and restart its time-out period; writing any other value resets the system at once.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Divides GCLK_RTC down to the counter clock CLK_RTC_CNT: 0x0 DIV1, 0x1 DIV2, 0x2 DIV4, 0x3 DIV8, 0x4 DIV16, 0x5 DIV32, 0x6 DIV64, 0x7 DIV128, 0x8 DIV256, 0x9 DIV512, 0xA DIV1024; 0xB-0xF reserved. Not synchronized.

fields.text: Clear on match; applies in Mode 0 and Mode 2 only. Not synchronized.

values.text: Counter keeps counting on a Compare/Alarm 0 match.

fields.name: MODE

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the RTC on or off after a synchronization delay: the written value reads back at once, STATUS.SYNCBUSY sets, and it clears when the change is done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every RTC register except DBGCTRL to its reset state and turn the RTC off; writing 0 does nothing. A 1 here wins over every other write in the same access, which is dropped. The reset finishes after a synchronization delay, when CTRL.SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both go to 0. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: RREQ
fields.text: Write 1 to ask for synchronization of the register READREQ.ADDR points to; this also sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RCONT
fields.text: Write 1 to keep the register READREQ.ADDR points to synchronized automatically on every update, and to stop READREQ.RREQ from clearing on its own; write 0 to stop. Goes to 0 when that register is written.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Offset of the register to be read-synchronized. Only COUNT and CLOCK, at one shared address, can be, so this is fixed at 0x10 and read-only.

values.text: An event on every Compare 0 match.

fields.name: PEREOx
fields.text: Periodic interval x event output enable, one bit per x from 0 to 7.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Overflow interrupt enable and so turn that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Overflow interrupt on; a request is raised when the Overflow flag sets.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Synchronization Ready interrupt enable and so turn that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Synchronization Ready interrupt on; a request is raised when its flag sets.

fields.name: CMP0
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Compare 0 interrupt enable and so turn that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Compare 0 interrupt on; a request is raised when its flag sets.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Overflow interrupt enable and turn that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Interrupt Flag Status and Clear - MODE0

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Goes to 1 one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after the counter overflows, raising an interrupt request if INTENCLR/SET.OVF is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Goes to 1 when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless the fall came from an enable or a software reset; with INTENCLR/SET.SYNCRDY at 1 this raises an interrupt request. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMP0
fields.text: Goes to 1 one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after the counter matches the compare condition, raising an interrupt request if INTENCLR/SET.CMP0 is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: 1 while registers are being synchronized between clock domains; goes to 0 when that finishes.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: 0 stops the RTC while in debug mode; 1 lets it keep running normally. A software reset leaves this bit unchanged.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Direction of the frequency correction.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: How much the RTC prescaler is corrected by; any value from 1 to 127 shifts the RTC frequency by an amount set by that value.

fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Current value of the 32-bit RTC counter.

registers.name: COMP
registers.title: Compare n Value - MODE0
notes: Also listed under the name COMP0.

fields.name: COMP
fields.text: 32-bit value compared all the time with COUNT. On a match, INTFLAG.CMPn sets one counter cycle later, and COUNT is reset to zero if CTRL.MATCHCLR is 1.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Divides GCLK_RTC to give the counter clock CLK_RTC_CNT; not synchronized. 0x0 DIV1 to 0xA DIV1024 divide by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 or 1024 in turn; 0xB-0xF are reserved.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Selects how the RTC runs; not synchronized. 0x0 COUNT32 makes it a 32-bit counter, 0x1 COUNT16 a 16-bit counter, 0x2 CLOCK a clock and calendar; 0x3 is reserved.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the RTC on or off after a synchronization delay: the written value reads back at once, STATUS.SYNCBUSY sets, and it clears when the change is complete. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every RTC register except DBGCTRL to its reset state and disables the RTC; other writes in the same operation are dropped. Writing 0 does nothing. SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY clear once the delayed reset finishes; not enable-protected.

fields.name: RREQ
fields.text: Writing 1 starts read synchronization of the register selected by READREQ.ADDR and sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RCONT
fields.text: 1 keeps the register at READREQ.ADDR synchronized automatically on every update and stops RREQ from self-clearing; 0 turns this off. Cleared when that register is written.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Offset of the register to read-synchronize. Only COUNT/CLOCK, sharing one address, can be read-synchronized, so this reads as the constant 0x10.

fields.name: OVFEO
fields.text: Overflow Event Output Enable.

fields.name: CMPEOx
fields.text: Compare x Event Output Enable.

values.text: An event on every compare x match.

fields.name: PEREOx
fields.text: Periodic Interval x Event Output Enable.

values.text: Periodic interval x events are generated.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the overflow interrupt enable, disabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Overflow interrupt on: a request is made when the overflow flag sets.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the synchronization ready interrupt enable, disabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Synchronization ready interrupt on: a request is made when its flag sets.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the compare x interrupt enable, disabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Compare x interrupt on: a request is made when its flag sets.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the overflow interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the synchronization ready interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the compare x interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Interrupt Flag Status and Clear - MODE1

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Sets one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after an overflow and requests an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.OVF is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Sets when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless enable or software reset caused it, and requests an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.SYNCRDY is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Sets one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after the compare x condition matches and requests an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.CMPx is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: 1 while registers are being synchronized between clock domains; goes to 0 when that finishes.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: 1 lets the RTC keep running in debug mode; 0 halts it there. A software reset leaves this bit alone.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Correction Sign.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: How much the RTC prescaler is corrected by; 1-127 adjust the RTC frequency by that amount.

fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Current value of the 16-bit RTC counter.

fields.name: PER
fields.text: Period of the 16-bit RTC counter.

fields.name: COMP
fields.text: 16-bit value compared all the time against COUNT; on a match, INTFLAG.CMPn sets on the following counter cycle.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Divides GCLK_RTC down to the counter clock CLK_RTC_CNT; not synchronized. 0x0 DIV1 through 0xA DIV1024: CLK_RTC_CNT is GCLK_RTC divided by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 or 1024 in turn; 0xB-0xF reserved.

fields.name: MATCHCLR
fields.text: Selects whether a Compare/Alarm 0 match resets the counter; applies in Mode 0 and Mode 2 only, writable only while the RTC is disabled, not synchronized.

values.text: Counter keeps running on a Compare/Alarm 0 match.
Counter is reset on a Compare/Alarm 0 match.

fields.name: CLKREP
fields.text: Picks the hour format used in CLOCK; applies in Mode 2 only, writable only while the RTC is disabled, not synchronized.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Chooses how the RTC operates; not synchronized. 0x0 COUNT32: 32-bit counter (Mode 0). 0x1 COUNT16: 16-bit counter (Mode 1). 0x2 CLOCK: clock/calendar (Mode 2). 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the RTC on or off. The written value reads back at once and STATUS.SYNCBUSY goes high until the change takes effect after synchronization, then clears. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every RTC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disable the RTC; writing 0 does nothing. A 1 here wins over the rest of the same write, whose other writes are dropped. The reset finishes after synchronization, when CTRL.SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both clear. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: RREQ
fields.text: Write 1 to start synchronizing the register at READREQ.ADDR, which also sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RCONT
fields.text: Write 1 to keep the register at READREQ.ADDR synchronized automatically on every update, and to stop READREQ.RREQ from clearing by itself; write 0 to end that. Cleared when the register at READREQ.ADDR is written.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Offset of the register to read-synchronize. Only COUNT and CLOCK, at the same address, can be read-synchronized in the RTC, so this field is fixed read-only at 0x10.

fields.name: OVFEO
fields.text: Enables the overflow event output.

values.text: An event is generated on each overflow.

fields.name: ALARMEO0
fields.text: Enables the Alarm 0 event output.

values.text: An event is generated on each Alarm 0 match.

fields.name: PEREOx
fields.text: Bit x enables the event output of Periodic Interval x.

values.text: No Periodic Interval x event is generated.
Periodic Interval x events are generated.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Overflow Interrupt Enable bit, turning the overflow interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing. Reads give the enable state.

values.text: Overflow interrupt on: a request is raised when the overflow flag sets.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the Synchronization Ready Interrupt Enable bit, turning that interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing. Reads give the enable state.

values.text: Synchronization ready interrupt on: a request is raised when its flag sets.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Alarm 0 interrupt off; writing 0 does nothing. Reads give the enable state.

values.text: Alarm 0 interrupt on: a request is raised when the Alarm 0 flag sets.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Overflow Interrupt Enable bit, turning the overflow interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing. Reads give the enable state.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Synchronization Ready interrupt enable, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing. Reads give the enable state.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Write 1 to set the Alarm 0 Interrupt Enable bit, turning the Alarm 0 interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing. Reads give the enable state.

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Interrupt Flag Status and Clear - MODE2

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Goes high one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after the counter overflows, and raises an interrupt request when INTENCLR/SET.OVF is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Goes high when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, except when that fall follows an enable or software reset, and raises an interrupt request when INTENCLR/SET.SYNCRDY is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Goes high one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after an ALARM0 match, and raises an interrupt request when INTENCLR/SET.ALARM0 is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: High while registers are being synchronized between the clock domains; goes high when synchronization starts and low when it finishes.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: 0 halts the RTC while in debug mode; 1 lets it keep running normally. A software reset leaves this bit unchanged.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Direction of the frequency correction.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: How much the RTC prescaler is corrected; 1 to 127 adjust the RTC frequency in line with the value.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Years counted from a reference year chosen by software; a year whose YEAR[1:0] is 0 is treated as a leap year.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Month, 1 for January up to 12 for December.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Day of the month, from 1 up to 28, 29, 30 or 31 as the month and year require.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Hour. With CTRL.CLKREP at 0 it runs 0 to 23 in 24-hour form; with CTRL.CLKREP at 1, HOUR[3:0] runs 1 to 12 and HOUR[4] is 0 for AM, 1 for PM. Settings: 0x10 PM, the afternoon hour; 0x0-0xF and 0x11-0x1F reserved.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Minute, 0 to 59.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Second, 0 to 59.

registers.name: ALARM
registers.title: Alarm n Value - MODE2
notes: ALARM0 is compared all the time with CLOCK, over the fields MASKn.SEL picks. On a match, INTFLAG.ALARMn sets on the following counter cycle, and the counter is cleared when CTRL.MATCHCLR is 1.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Year to alarm on; compared only when MASKn.SEL is 6.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Month to alarm on; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 4.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Day to alarm on; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 3.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Hour to alarm on; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 2.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Minute to alarm on; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 1.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Second to alarm on; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 0.

fields.name: SEL
fields.text: Chooses which parts of Alarm n take part in the match. 0x0 OFF: alarm off. 0x1 SS: seconds. 0x2 MMSS: seconds, minutes. 0x3 HHMMSS: adds hours. 0x4 DDHHMMSS: adds days. 0x5 MMDDHHMMSS: adds months. 0x6 YYMMDDHHMMSS: adds years. 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: LVLENx
fields.text: Lets requests of priority level x reach the arbiter when 1; they are ignored when 0. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: CRCENABLE
fields.text: A 1 turns the CRC module on. A 0 turns it off only while CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY is 0; with CRCBUSY at 1 the write is ignored and the module stays on. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: DMAENABLE
fields.text: A 1 turns the DMAC on. A 0 during a transfer takes effect only once the internal transfer buffer has emptied, at the end of the current burst, and the transfer is aborted. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A 1, accepted only while DMAENABLE and CRCENABLE are both 0, returns every DMAC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value; with either module on the request is ignored and the DMAC returns an access error. A 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CRCSRC
fields.text: Picks what feeds the CRC; locked, with CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY showing the lock, until generation finishes or the CRC module is turned off. With a DMA channel as source, that channel signals completion. 0x0 NOACT: none; 0x1 IO: fed from the I/O interface; 0x2-0x1F reserved; 0x20-0x3F CHN: fed from DMA channel n.

fields.name: CRCPOLY
fields.text: Picks the CRC polynomial. 0x0 CRC16: CRC-16 (CRC-CCITT); 0x1 CRC32: CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3); 0x2-0x3 reserved.

fields.name: CRCBEATSIZE
fields.text: Width of each bus access when the CRC is fed from the I/O interface. 0x0 BYTE: 8-bit; 0x1 HWORD: 16-bit; 0x2 WORD: 32-bit; 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: CRCDATAIN
fields.text: Data word to run through the CRC. After a write, the time until the new checksum is ready depends on CRCCTRL.CRCBEATSIZE: one clock cycle per byte.

fields.name: CRCCHKSUM
fields.text: The CRC result; the upper 16 bits read 0 in CRC-16 mode. Valid once CRCSTATUS.BUSY is 0: a plain checksum for CRC-16, a bit-reversed one for CRC-32 (bit 31 swapped with bit 0, bit 30 with bit 1, and so on).

fields.name: CRCZERO
fields.text: Set when CRC generation ends with a zero checksum; cleared when a new CRC source is chosen.

fields.name: CRCBUSY
fields.text: CRC busy. From the I/O interface (CRCCTRL.CRCSRC = 0x1): set by a write to CRCDATAIN, cleared by writing 1. From a DMA channel (CRCSRC = 0x20-0x3F): set when that channel is enabled, cleared when it is disabled, and writing 1 does nothing. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Sets what the DMAC does while an external debugger halts the CPU. A software reset leaves it unchanged.

values.text: DMAC stops while the CPU is halted by the debugger.
DMAC keeps running while the CPU is halted by the debugger.

fields.name: DQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority during data transfer. 0x0 DISABLE: background, nothing sensitive; 0x1 LOW: bandwidth-sensitive; 0x2 MEDIUM: latency-sensitive; 0x3 HIGH: latency-critical.

fields.name: FQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority during descriptor fetch. 0x0 DISABLE: background, nothing sensitive; 0x1 LOW: bandwidth-sensitive; 0x2 MEDIUM: latency-sensitive; 0x3 HIGH: latency-critical.

fields.name: WRBQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority during write-back. 0x0 DISABLE: background, nothing sensitive; 0x1 LOW: bandwidth-sensitive; 0x2 MEDIUM: latency-sensitive; 0x3 HIGH: latency-critical.

fields.name: SWTRIGx
fields.text: A 1 starts a software trigger on channel x when its CHSTATUS.PEND is 0; if PEND is already 1 the bit is set instead. Cleared when that channel's CHSTATUS.PEND sets, or by writing 0 or 1 to it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN3
fields.text: Picks the scheduling scheme for priority level 3.

fields.name: LVLPRI3
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 3 (PRICTRL0.RRLVLEN3 = 1), holds the number of the last level-3 channel granted access. With static arbitration (RRLVLEN3 = 0), a nonzero value x gives channel x top priority, falling through x+1 up to the last channel n, then channel 0 (below n) down to x-1. Not reset when RRLVLEN3 is written to 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN2
fields.text: Picks the scheduling scheme for priority level 2.

fields.name: LVLPRI2
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 2 (PRICTRL0.RRLVLEN2 = 1), holds the number of the last level-2 channel granted access. With static arbitration (RRLVLEN2 = 0), a nonzero value x gives channel x top priority, falling through x+1 up to the last channel n, then channel 0 (below n) down to x-1. Not reset when RRLVLEN2 is written to 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN1
fields.text: Picks the scheduling scheme for priority level 1.

fields.name: LVLPRI1
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 1 (PRICTRL0.RRLVLEN1 = 1), holds the number of the last level-1 channel granted access. With static arbitration (RRLVLEN1 = 0), a nonzero value x gives channel x top priority, falling through x+1 up to the last channel n, then channel 0 (below n) down to x-1. Not reset when RRLVLEN1 is written to 0.

fields.name: RRLVLEN0
fields.text: Picks the scheduling scheme for priority level 0.

fields.name: LVLPRI0
fields.text: With round-robin on for level 0 (PRICTRL0.RRLVLEN0 = 1), holds the number of the last level-0 channel granted access. With static arbitration (RRLVLEN0 = 0), a nonzero value x gives channel x top priority, falling through x+1 up to the last channel n, then channel 0 (below n) down to x-1. Not reset when RRLVLEN0 is written to 0.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Reads 1 while the channel named in ID is pending.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 while the channel named in ID is busy.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID has fetched an invalid descriptor.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID has a Suspend interrupt waiting; writing 1 clears that channel's Suspend flag, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID has a Transfer Complete interrupt waiting; writing 1 clears that flag, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named in ID has a Transfer Error interrupt waiting; writing 1 clears that flag, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Lowest-numbered channel with an interrupt waiting, valid while SUSP, TCMPL or TERR is set. Updated when a lower-numbered channel gets an interrupt or the current one's sources are cleared; reads 0 with none waiting. Writing it opens indirect access to that channel's interrupt flag register.

fields.name: CHINTx
fields.text: Set while channel x has an interrupt waiting; cleared when its interrupts are disabled or their sources cleared.

fields.name: BUSYCHx
fields.text: Set when channel x starts a transfer; cleared when its trigger action finishes, on a bus error on it, or when it is disabled.

fields.name: PENDCHx
fields.text: Set while a transfer waits on channel x; cleared when its trigger action begins executing, on a bus error on it, or when it is disabled.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit block transfer count of the transfer in progress, held in the active channel and written back to that channel's write-back location when the arbiter grants another channel. Valid only while ABUSY is 1.

fields.name: ABUSY
fields.text: Set when the next descriptor's transfer count is read from write-back memory; cleared when the active count is written back there.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Number of the channel now held in the active channel registers, updated at every new grant by the arbiter.

fields.name: LVLEXx
fields.text: 1 while a trigger request from a level-x channel is running or waiting.

fields.name: BASEADDR
fields.text: Base address of the descriptor memory; must be 128-bit aligned.

fields.name: WRBADDR
fields.text: Base address of the write-back memory; must be 128-bit aligned.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Number of the channel the channel registers reach; write it before reading or writing any channel register.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: A 1 turns the channel on. A 0 during a transfer takes effect only once the internal transfer buffer has emptied, at the end of the current burst, and the transfer is aborted. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A 1 returns the channel's registers to their reset values; accepted only while ENABLE is 0, ignored while it is 1. Clears itself when the reset is done. A 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Software command to the channel. Not enable-protected. 0x0 NOACT: none; 0x1 SUSPEND: suspend the channel; 0x2 RESUME: resume the channel; 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: TRIGACT
fields.text: What one trigger starts. 0x0 BLOCK: one block; 0x1 reserved; 0x2 BEAT: one beat; 0x3 TRANSACTION: one whole transaction.

fields.name: TRIGSRC
fields.text: Peripheral trigger that starts the channel's transfer.

fields.name: LVL
fields.text: Arbitration level of the channel; a higher level wins over a lower one. Not enable-protected. 0x0 LVL0: level 0; 0x1 LVL1: level 1; 0x2 LVL2: level 2; 0x3 LVL3: level 3.

fields.name: EVOE
fields.text: Turns on the channel's event output, which fires on each condition chosen by the descriptor's BTCTRL.EVOSEL. Present only on channels that have an event output.

fields.name: EVIE
fields.text: Turns on the channel's event input. Present only on channels that have an event input.

values.text: Each incoming event triggers the channel's event action.

fields.name: EVACT
fields.text: Action taken on an input event, only while CHCTRLB.EVIE is 1 and only on channels with an event input. 0x0 NOACT: none; 0x1 TRIG: starts a transfer or periodic transfer; 0x2 CTRIG: starts a transfer conditionally; 0x3 CBLOCK: block transfer, conditional; 0x4 SUSPEND: channel suspends; 0x5 RESUME: channel resumes; 0x6 SSKIP: next block suspend action skipped; 0x7 reserved.

values.name: TRIG
values.text: Triggers a transfer or periodic transfer.

values.name: SSKIP
values.text: Skips the next block suspend action.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the channel Suspend interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the channel Transfer Complete interrupt; writing 0 does nothing. With the block action set to none, the TCMPL flag is not set when a block finishes.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the channel Transfer Error interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the channel Suspend interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the channel Transfer Complete interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the channel Transfer Error interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTFLAG
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Set when a block with the suspend block action finishes, on a software suspend command, on a suspend event, or on an invalid descriptor fetch. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Set when a block finishes and its block action includes the interrupt. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Set on a bus error during a beat or on an invalid descriptor fetch. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Set when an invalid descriptor is fetched; cleared by a software resume command.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Set when the channel starts a transfer; cleared when its trigger action finishes, on a bus error, or when it is disabled.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Set while a transfer waits on the channel; cleared when its trigger action begins executing, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: STEPSIZE
fields.text: Address step on each beat, applied to the source or the destination as STEPSEL picks: next address = address + BEATSIZE x step. 0x0 X1: 1; 0x1 X2: 2; 0x2 X4: 4; 0x3 X8: 8; 0x4 X16: 16; 0x5 X32: 32; 0x6 X64: 64; 0x7 X128: 128.

values.name: X1
values.text: Next address is address + BEATSIZE x 1.

values.name: X2
values.text: Next address is address + BEATSIZE x 2.

values.name: X4
values.text: Next address is address + BEATSIZE x 4.

values.name: X8
values.text: Next address is address + BEATSIZE x 8.

values.name: X16
values.text: Next address is address + BEATSIZE x 16.

values.name: X32
values.text: Next address is address + BEATSIZE x 32.

values.name: X64
values.text: Next address is address + BEATSIZE x 64.

values.name: X128
values.text: Next address is address + BEATSIZE x 128.

fields.name: STEPSEL
fields.text: Which address STEPSIZE applies to. 0x0 DST: destination; 0x1 SRC: source.

values.name: DST
values.text: Step applies to the destination address.

values.name: SRC
values.text: Step applies to the source address.

fields.name: DSTINC
fields.text: A 1 makes the destination address advance, by 1 unless STEPSEL is 0, in which case STEPSIZE sets the step; a 0 holds it fixed for the whole transfer.

fields.name: SRCINC
fields.text: A 1 makes the source address advance, by 1 unless STEPSEL is 1, in which case STEPSIZE sets the step; a 0 holds it fixed for the whole transfer.

fields.name: BEATSIZE
fields.text: Size of one beat, one bus access, used for both reads and writes. 0x0 BYTE: 8-bit; 0x1 HWORD: 16-bit; 0x2 WORD: 32-bit; 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: BLOCKACT
fields.text: What the DMAC does when a block finishes. 0x0 NOACT: nothing; 0x1 INT: block interrupt, channel carries on; 0x2 SUSPEND: channel suspends; 0x3 BOTH: channel suspends and block interrupt.

values.name: INT
values.text: Block interrupt; channel runs on normally.

fields.name: EVOSEL
fields.text: When the channel puts out an event. 0x0 DISABLE: never; 0x1 BLOCK: a strobe at each finished block; 0x2 reserved; 0x3 BEAT: a strobe at each finished beat.

fields.name: VALID
fields.text: A descriptor holding 0 here, in descriptor or write-back memory, suspends the channel when it is fetched. Cleared by hardware in write-back memory when the channel is aborted, an error occurs during the block, or the block finishes.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit block transfer count, counted down by one after each beat. The running count goes to the channel's write-back location when the channel loses priority, is suspended or is disabled (by finishing, by a transfer error, or by software).

fields.name: SRCADDR
fields.text: Source address of the last beat in the block.

fields.name: DSTADDR
fields.text: Destination address of the last beat in the block.

fields.name: DESCADDR
fields.text: SRAM address of the next descriptor, 128-bit aligned. A value of 0x00000000 ends the transaction when the DMAC goes to load the next descriptor.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the EIC on or off. The written value reads back at once and sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY; the change takes effect after synchronization, when SYNCBUSY clears.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A 1 returns every EIC register to its reset value and turns the EIC off; it overrides any other write in the same access. The reset finishes after synchronization, when SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both clear. A 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: Set when register synchronization between the clock domains begins; cleared when it is done.

fields.name: NMIFILTEN
fields.text: Non-maskable interrupt filter enable.

fields.name: NMISENSE
fields.text: Picks the edge or level of the NMI pin that triggers the NMI. 0x0 NONE: no detection; 0x1 RISE: rising edge; 0x2 FALL: falling edge; 0x3 BOTH: either edge; 0x4 HIGH: high level; 0x5 LOW: low level; 0x6-0x7 reserved.

registers.name: NMIFLAG
registers.title: Non-Maskable Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: NMI
fields.text: Set when the NMI pin matches the NMISENSE setting, raising an interrupt request. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTEOx
fields.text: Turns on an event from pin EXTINTx at each detection.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the External Interrupt x enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the External Interrupt x enable bit, turning that interrupt on; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: Set when pin EXTINTx matches its sense setting; it then requests an interrupt provided INTENCLR/SET.EXTINT[x] reads 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WAKEUPENx
fields.text: Lets pin EXTINTx wake the device from sleep when it matches its sense setting.

registers.name: CONFIG
registers.title: Configuration n
notes: The heading for FILTENx leaves out bit 3, the diagram's FILTEN0.
The heading for SENSEx leaves out bits 2:0, the diagram's SENSE0.
Also listed under the name CONFIG0.

fields.name: FILTEN7
fields.text: Turns on the input filter for EXTINT7.

fields.name: SENSE7
fields.text: Picks the edge or level of EXTINT7 that raises its interrupt or event. 0x0 NONE: no detection; 0x1 RISE: rising edge; 0x2 FALL: falling edge; 0x3 BOTH: either edge; 0x4 HIGH: high level; 0x5 LOW: low level; 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN6
fields.text: Turns on the input filter for EXTINT6.

fields.name: SENSE6
fields.text: Picks the edge or level of EXTINT6 that raises its interrupt or event. 0x0 NONE: no detection; 0x1 RISE: rising edge; 0x2 FALL: falling edge; 0x3 BOTH: either edge; 0x4 HIGH: high level; 0x5 LOW: low level; 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN5
fields.text: Turns on the input filter for EXTINT5.

fields.name: SENSE5
fields.text: Picks the edge or level of EXTINT5 that raises its interrupt or event. 0x0 NONE: no detection; 0x1 RISE: rising edge; 0x2 FALL: falling edge; 0x3 BOTH: either edge; 0x4 HIGH: high level; 0x5 LOW: low level; 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN4
fields.text: Turns on the input filter for EXTINT4.

fields.name: SENSE4
fields.text: Picks the edge or level of EXTINT4 that raises its interrupt or event. 0x0 NONE: no detection; 0x1 RISE: rising edge; 0x2 FALL: falling edge; 0x3 BOTH: either edge; 0x4 HIGH: high level; 0x5 LOW: low level; 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN3
fields.text: Turns on the input filter for EXTINT3.

fields.name: SENSE3
fields.text: Picks the edge or level of EXTINT3 that raises its interrupt or event. 0x0 NONE: no detection; 0x1 RISE: rising edge; 0x2 FALL: falling edge; 0x3 BOTH: either edge; 0x4 HIGH: high level; 0x5 LOW: low level; 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN2
fields.text: Turns on the input filter for EXTINT2.

fields.name: SENSE2
fields.text: Picks the edge or level of EXTINT2 that raises its interrupt or event. 0x0 NONE: no detection; 0x1 RISE: rising edge; 0x2 FALL: falling edge; 0x3 BOTH: either edge; 0x4 HIGH: high level; 0x5 LOW: low level; 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN1
fields.text: Turns on the input filter for EXTINT1.

fields.name: SENSE1
fields.text: Picks the edge or level of EXTINT1 that raises its interrupt or event. 0x0 NONE: no detection; 0x1 RISE: rising edge; 0x2 FALL: falling edge; 0x3 BOTH: either edge; 0x4 HIGH: high level; 0x5 LOW: low level; 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN0
fields.text: Turns on the input filter for EXTINT0.

fields.name: SENSE0
fields.text: Picks the edge or level of EXTINT0 that raises its interrupt or event. 0x0 NONE: no detection; 0x1 RISE: rising edge; 0x2 FALL: falling edge; 0x3 BOTH: either edge; 0x4 HIGH: high level; 0x5 LOW: low level; 0x6-0x7 reserved.

fields.name: CMDEX
fields.text: Key that lets the command in CMD run: 0xA5 executes it; any other key blocks the write and sets STATUS.PROGE, as does a write while an earlier command is still running. Write it together with CMD, and only while READY is 1. An APB command arriving in the same cycle as an AHB access waits until the AHB access and the NVM block are idle. Bit 0 reads 1 until the command has been issued. 0xA5: KEY, execution key; 0x00-0xA4 and 0xA6-0xFF: reserved.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Command that runs when the CMDEX key is written alongside it.

values.name: ER
values.text: Erase row: erases the row at the address in ADDR.

values.name: WP
values.text: Write page: writes the page buffer into the page at the address in ADDR.

values.name: EAR
values.text: Erase auxiliary row: erases the auxiliary row at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear and only for the user configuration row.

values.name: WAP
values.text: Write auxiliary page: writes the page buffer into the auxiliary page at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear and only for the user configuration row.

values.name: LR
values.text: Lock region: locks the region holding the address in ADDR.

values.name: UR
values.text: Unlock region: unlocks the region holding the address in ADDR.

values.name: SSB
values.text: Set security bit: writes 0x00 into the first byte of the lockbit row, which sets the security bit.

fields.name: CACHEDIS
fields.text: Turns the NVM cache off.

fields.name: READMODE
fields.text: How the cache handles misses. 0x0 NO_MISS_PENALTY: no wait state added on a miss; highest system performance. 0x1 LOW_POWER: the cache uses less power but adds a wait state on every miss, stalling the CPU and possibly lengthening run time. 0x2 DETERMINISTIC: a hit and a miss take the same time, set by the programmed flash wait states, for real-time code needing fixed timing. 0x3: reserved.

values.name: NO_MISS_PENALTY
values.text: No wait state on a cache miss; best system performance.

values.name: LOW_POWER
values.text: Lower cache power, with a wait state added on every miss; the stalled CPU may run longer.

values.name: DETERMINISTIC
values.text: Hit and miss take equal time, set by the programmed flash wait states; for real-time code.

fields.name: SLEEPPRM
fields.text: NVM power reduction mode in sleep. 0x0 WAKEONACCESS: the NVM block goes low-power on entering sleep and leaves it at the first access. 0x1 WAKEUPINSTANT: the NVM block goes low-power on entering sleep and leaves it on leaving sleep. 0x2: reserved. 0x3 DISABLED: no automatic power reduction.

values.name: WAKEONACCESS
values.text: Low-power on entering sleep; out of it at the first access.

values.name: WAKEUPINSTANT
values.text: Low-power on entering sleep; out of it on leaving sleep.

fields.name: MANW
fields.text: Manual write: whether a page write, to main memory or an auxiliary row, starts on its own or only by a command in CMD.

values.text: Filling the last word of the page buffer starts a write to the page the previous write went to, for main memory and auxiliary rows alike.
Writes start only from a command in CMD.

fields.name: RWS
fields.text: Wait states inserted on each NVM read, 0 to 15; resets to 0. Software may change it to suit the NVM access time and the system clock.

fields.name: PSZ
fields.text: NVM page size: 0x0 8 bytes, 0x1 16, 0x2 32, 0x3 64, 0x4 128, 0x5 256, 0x6 512, 0x7 1024 bytes. A device family may not offer every size.

fields.name: NVMP
fields.text: How many pages the main NVM address space holds.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the ERROR interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads back the ERROR interrupt enable.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the READY interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads back the READY interrupt enable.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the ERROR interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads back the ERROR interrupt enable.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the READY interrupt; 0 does nothing. Reads back the READY interrupt enable.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Goes to 1 on any NVME, LOCKE or PROGE error; write 1 to clear it.

values.text: No error since it was last cleared.
One or more errors since it was last cleared.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: NVM ready.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Security bit status.

fields.name: NVME
fields.text: NVM error flag; write 1 to clear it.

values.text: No program or erase error reported by the NVM controller since it was last cleared.
The NVM controller reported one or more errors since it was last cleared.

fields.name: LOCKE
fields.text: Lock error flag; write 1 to clear it.

values.text: No locked region has been programmed since it was last cleared.
A locked region has been programmed since it was last cleared.

fields.name: PROGE
fields.text: Programming error flag; write 1 to clear it.

values.text: No invalid command or wrong key written to the command register since it was last cleared.
An invalid command or a wrong key, or both, was written to the command register since it was last cleared.

fields.name: LOAD
fields.text: Shows the page buffer holds one or more loaded words: set right after a load, held until a page write or page buffer clear (PBCLR) command. Write 1 to clear it.

fields.name: PRM
fields.text: Current NVM power reduction state. It is entered by command or on entering sleep with a suitable SLEEPPRM; it is left on an AHB access to the NVM block, by command (SPRM, CPRM), or on leaving sleep with a suitable SLEEPPRM.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: 16-bit hardware address given to the NVM when CMDEX runs a command, as an offset within the addressed section. Shift a byte address right by one before writing it. Updated by writes to the page buffer and may also be written directly.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: One lock bit per region; set and cleared only through commands in CMD.

registers.name: DIRn
registers.title: Data Direction
notes: Also listed under the name DIR.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Direction of each I/O pin in the group.

registers.name: DIRCLRn
registers.title: Data Direction Clear
notes: Also listed under the name DIRCLR.

fields.name: DIRCLR
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the matching DIR bit, making that pin an input; 0 does nothing.

registers.name: DIRSETn
registers.title: Data Direction Set
notes: Also listed under the name DIRSET.

fields.name: DIRSET
fields.text: Write 1 to set the matching DIR bit, making that pin an output; 0 does nothing.

registers.name: DIRTGLn
registers.title: Data Direction Toggle
notes: Also listed under the name DIRTGL.

fields.name: DIRTGL
fields.text: Write 1 to flip the matching DIR bit, reversing that pin's direction; 0 does nothing.

registers.name: OUTn
registers.title: Data Output Value
notes: Also listed under the name OUT.

fields.name: OUT
fields.text: Output level of each pin set as an output by DIR; for an input pin with PULLEN on, picks pull-up or pull-down.

values.text: Drives low, or pulls the input down.
Drives high, or pulls the input up.

registers.name: OUTCLRn
registers.title: Data Output Value Clear
notes: Also listed under the name OUTCLR.

fields.name: OUTCLR
fields.text: Write 1 to clear the matching OUT bit: an output pin goes low, an input pin with PULLEN on gets a pull-down. 0 does nothing.

registers.name: OUTSETn
registers.title: Data Output Value Set
notes: Also listed under the name OUTSET.

fields.name: OUTSET
fields.text: Write 1 to set the matching OUT bit: an output pin goes high, an input pin with PULLEN on gets a pull-up. 0 does nothing.

registers.name: OUTTGLn
registers.title: Data Output Value Toggle
notes: Also listed under the name OUTTGL.

fields.name: OUTTGL
fields.text: Write 1 to flip the matching OUT bit: an output pin changes level, an input pin with PULLEN on swaps its pull direction. 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INn
registers.title: Data Input Value
notes: Also listed under the name IN.

fields.name: IN
fields.text: Sampled level of each pin: 0 when the input sampler sees low, 1 when it sees high.

registers.name: CTRLn
registers.title: Control
notes: Also listed under the name CTRL.

fields.name: SAMPLING
fields.text: Input sampling for pins set as inputs by DIR. Samplers switch on and off in groups of eight: one pin of a byte asking for continuous sampling makes all eight pins of that byte sampled continuously.

registers.name: WRCONFIGn
registers.title: Write Configuration
notes: Also listed under the name WRCONFIG.

fields.name: HWSEL
fields.text: Picks which half of the 32-pin group the atomic write configures. Reads 0.

fields.name: WRPINCFG
fields.text: Write 1 to load the written DRVSTR, SLEWLIM, ODRAIN, PULLEN, INEN, PMUXEN and PINMASK values into PINCFGy of every pin chosen by PINMASK and HWSEL; 0 does nothing. Reads 0.

fields.name: WRPMUX
fields.text: Write 1 to load the written WRCONFIG.PMUX value into PMUXn of every pin chosen by PINMASK and HWSEL; 0 does nothing. Reads 0.

fields.name: PMUX
fields.text: Value written to PMUXn of the pins chosen by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPMUX is 1. Reads 0.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Value written to PINCFGy.DRVSTR of the pins chosen by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is 1. Reads 0.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Value written to PINCFGy.PULLEN of the pins chosen by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is 1. Reads 0.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Value written to PINCFGy.INEN of the pins chosen by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is 1. Reads 0.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Value written to PINCFGy.PMUXEN of the pins chosen by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is 1. Reads 0.

fields.name: PINMASK
fields.text: Chooses which pins of the half chosen by HWSEL get configured. Reads 0.

fields.name: PMUXO
fields.text: Peripheral function of odd pin 2n+1 when its PINCFGy.PMUXEN is 1; not every code may be valid. 0x0-0x7: functions A to H; 0x8-0xF: reserved.

fields.name: PMUXE
fields.text: Peripheral function of even pin 2n when its PINCFGy.PMUXEN is 1; not every code may be valid. 0x0-0x7: functions A to H; 0x8-0xF: reserved.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Drive strength of a pin set as an output.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Turns on the internal pull-up or pull-down of a pin set as an input.

values.text: No pull; the input floats at high impedance.
Pull on; the input sits at a set level when nothing drives it.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Turns on the pin's input buffer, for inputs and outputs alike. With it off the pin's level cannot be read back in either direction.

values.text: Buffer off; the input is not sampled.
Buffer on; the input is sampled when needed.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Hands the pin to the peripheral chosen in PMUXn. At 0, DIR and OUT set the pin's direction and level and PMUXn is ignored. At 1, the chosen peripheral drives the pin; its level can still be read in IN when PINCFGy.INEN is 1.

values.text: PORT registers set direction and drive.
The chosen peripheral sets direction and drive.

fields.name: GCLKREQ
fields.text: Chooses whether each channel's generic clock stays on permanently or is requested only when an event calls for it. Events on asynchronous paths need no generic clock.

values.text: Clock requested only when an event is detected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every EVSYS register to its reset state; 0 does nothing. It wins over everything else written in the same access, which is dropped.

fields.name: EDGSEL
fields.text: Edge detection on the channel, for the resynchronized and synchronous paths; write 0 when the path is asynchronous. 0x0 NO_EVT_OUTPUT: no event output. 0x1 RISING_EDGE: rising edges of the generator signal only. 0x2 FALLING_EDGE: falling edges only. 0x3 BOTH_EDGES: rising and falling edges.

values.name: NO_EVT_OUTPUT
values.text: No event output on the resynchronized or synchronous path.

values.name: RISING_EDGE
values.text: Rising edges of the generator signal only, on the resynchronized or synchronous path.

values.name: FALLING_EDGE
values.text: Falling edges of the generator signal only, on the resynchronized or synchronous path.

values.name: BOTH_EDGES
values.text: Rising and falling edges of the generator signal, on the resynchronized or synchronous path.

fields.name: PATH
fields.text: Path the channel uses; the event source may limit the choice. 0x0 SYNCHRONOUS, 0x1 RESYNCHRONIZED, 0x2 ASYNCHRONOUS, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: EVGEN
fields.text: Event generator connected to the channel.

rows: Compare 0 in modes 0 and 1, alarm 0 in mode 2.

fields.name: SWEVT
fields.text: Write 1 to fire a software event on the channel named in CHANNEL.CHANNEL; 0 does nothing. Write it with CHANNEL.CHANNEL in one 16-bit access. Reads 0.

fields.name: CHANNEL
fields.text: Channel to configure or read back.

fields.name: CHANNEL
fields.text: Channel connected to the event user, written as channel number plus one. 0x0: no channel. 0x1-0x5: channel n-1. 0x2-0xFF: reserved.

fields.name: USER
fields.text: Event user to configure with a channel or to read the channel from.

fields.name: CHBUSYx
fields.text: 1 while an event on channel x has not yet been handled by every user connected to it; 0 when the channel is idle.

fields.name: USRRDYx
fields.text: 1 when every user connected to channel x is ready for new events; 0 when one or more is not.

fields.name: EVDx
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the channel x event detected interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVRx
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the channel x overrun interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EVDx
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the channel x event detected interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVRx
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the channel x overrun interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EVDx
fields.text: Set one CLK_EVSYS_APB cycle after an event passes through channel x, raising an interrupt if EVDx is enabled; never set on an asynchronous path. Write 1 to clear it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVRx
fields.text: Set one CLK_EVSYS cycle after an overrun on channel x, raising an interrupt if OVRx is enabled; never set on an asynchronous path. Write 1 to clear it; 0 does nothing.

peripherals.name: SERCOM USART
peripherals.title: SERCOM Universal Synchronous and Asynchronous Receiver and Transmitter

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Order in which a character's bits leave the Data register. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: In synchronous mode, sets which XCK edge changes TxD and which samples RxD: 0 changes on rising and samples on falling, 1 changes on falling and samples on rising. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CMODE
fields.text: Picks asynchronous or synchronous operation. Not synchronized.

fields.name: FORM
fields.text: Selects the frame format. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SAMPA
fields.text: Sample adjustment: which over-sampled clocks the receiver samples on, at 16x and at 8x over-sampling. Not synchronized.

fields.name: RXPO
fields.text: Selects the SERCOM pad that receives data (RxD). Not synchronized.

fields.name: TXPO
fields.text: Selects the pads for TxD and XCK, and for RTS and CTS where they are used. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SAMPR
fields.text: Selects over-sampling and how the baud rate is generated. Not synchronized.

fields.name: IBON
fields.text: Chooses when STATUS.BUFOVF is raised after a buffer overflow.

values.text: Raised at its place in the data stream.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Behaviour in standby sleep. 0x0: with external clock, the clock is disconnected once the ongoing transfer ends and all reception is dropped; with internal clock, the generic clock stops once the ongoing transfer ends and Receive Start or Transfer Complete can wake the device. 0x1: with external clock, Receive Start or Receive Complete wakes the device; with internal clock, the generic clock runs in every sleep mode and any interrupt can wake the device. Not synchronized.

rows: Once the transfer in progress ends, the external clock is cut off and anything received is discarded.
Once the transfer in progress ends, the generic clock stops; the device wakes on a Receive Start or Transfer Complete interrupt.
A Receive Start or Receive Complete interrupt wakes the device.
The generic clock keeps running in every sleep mode; any interrupt can wake the device.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Write 0x0 or 0x1 to make the SERCOM a USART. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the SERCOM on or off. The change lands after synchronization: the written value reads back at once, SYNCBUSY.ENABLE is set, and it clears when the change is done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every SERCOM register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disable the SERCOM; writing 0 does nothing. It overrides every other write in the same access. Register writes during the reset give an APB error and reads return reset values. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when the reset is done. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Turns the receiver on or off. Writing 0 turns it off, empties the receive buffer and clears STATUS.FERR, PERR and BUFOVF. Writing 1 with the USART disabled sets the bit at once; with the USART enabled, the bit reads 0 and SYNCBUSY.CTRLB stays set until the receiver is on, then the bit reads 1. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Receiver on, or on once the USART is enabled.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Turns the transmitter on or off. Writing 0 takes effect only after ongoing and pending transmissions finish. Writing 1 with the USART disabled sets the bit at once; with the USART enabled, the bit reads 0 and SYNCBUSY.CTRLB stays set until the transmitter is on, then the bit reads 1. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Transmitter on, or on once the USART is enabled.

fields.name: PMODE
fields.text: Even or odd parity, used when CTRLA.FORM enables parity. The transmitter adds the parity bit to each frame; the receiver checks it and sets STATUS.PERR on a mismatch. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENC
fields.text: Selects the data encoding. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SFDE
fields.text: Lets the start-of-frame detector wake the device when a start bit appears on RxD; which of RXC and RXS wakes it follows INTENSET.RXS and INTENSET.RXC. Not synchronized.

values.text: On; RXC wakes from every sleep mode (RXS 0, RXC 1).
On; RXS wakes from every sleep mode (RXS 1, RXC 0).
On; RXC and RXS both wake from every sleep mode (RXS 1, RXC 1).

fields.name: COLDEN
fields.text: Collision Detection Enable: 0 leaves collision detection off, 1 turns it on. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SBMODE
fields.text: Number of stop bits sent. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CHSIZE
fields.text: Number of bits in a character. Not synchronized.

fields.name: FP[2:0]/BAUD
fields.text: Fractional part of the baud value, for clock generation.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Baud value, for clock generation.

fields.name: RXPL
fields.text: With IrDA encoding (CTRLB.ENC=1), the shortest pulse the IrDA receiver accepts, in serial engine clock periods: PULSE >= (RXPL + 1) x SE period.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Error interrupt off by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Receive Break interrupt off by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Clear To Send Input Change interrupt off by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Clear To Send Input Change interrupt off.
Clear To Send Input Change interrupt on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Receive Start interrupt off by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Receive Complete interrupt off by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Transmit Complete interrupt off by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Data Register Empty interrupt off by clearing its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Error interrupt on by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Receive Break interrupt on by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Clear To Send Input Change interrupt on by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Clear To Send Input Change interrupt off.
Clear To Send Input Change interrupt on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Receive Start interrupt on by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Receive Complete interrupt on by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Transmit Complete interrupt on by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Data Register Empty interrupt on by setting its enable; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Set when any error is found: COLL, ISF, BUFOVF, FERR or PERR, each with its own flag in STATUS. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Set when a break character arrives with auto-baud enabled in CTRLA.FORM. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Set when the CTS pin changes. Write 1 to clear; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXS

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Writing CMD starts a slave operation; the bits are strobes and read as 0. What a command does depends on INTFLAG.DRDY, INTFLAG.AMATCH and STATUS.DIR, and any command clears INTFLAG.DRDY, INTFLAG.AMATCH and INTFLAG.PREC. 0x2 after a data interrupt (DRDY): on a master write, does the acknowledge action and then waits for any START or repeated START; on a master read, waits for any START or repeated START. 0x3 after an address interrupt (AMATCH): on a master write, does the acknowledge action and then takes in the next byte; on a master read, does the acknowledge action and then raises the slave data interrupt. 0x3 after a data interrupt (DRDY): on a master write, does the acknowledge action and then takes in the next byte; on a master read, reads a byte and then takes the ACK or NACK. fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: Sets when a slave byte transfer completes. Hardware clears it on a write to DATA, a read of DATA with smart mode on, or a valid write to CMD; writing 1 also clears it, and writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: AMATCH
fields.text: Sets when the address logic sees a valid matching address. Hardware clears it when CMD is written; writing 1 also clears it, and writing 0 does nothing. Clearing it sends ACK or NACK as CTRLB.ACKACT sets.

fields.name: PREC
fields.text: Sets when a STOP is seen for a transaction this slave is handling; a STOP between the master and another slave does not set it. Hardware clears it after a command on the next address match; writing 1 also clears it, and writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Sets when the slave sees a START followed by a master code. Writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing, and a received STOP clears it too.

Cleared by answering an address match with ACK or NACK (CTRLB.CMD = 0x3), by clearing INTFLAG.AMATCH, or by writing 1; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MB

If arbitration was not lost, the master then holds SCL low. SCL is released and MB clears on a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or a valid write to CTRLB.CMD. Writing 1 clears MB, but the transaction neither goes on nor ends until one of those actions happens. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: MEXTTOUT

fields.name: LOWTOUT

fields.name: BUSSTATE

notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xxxxxxxx.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Data buffer address in RAM, as an absolute word address; bits 1:0 must be zero so the start is 32-bit aligned.

registers.name: PCKSIZE
registers.title: Packet Size
notes: The bit diagram also spells BYTE_COUNT as BYTE-COUNT.

fields.name: AUTO_ZLP
fields.text: Lets hardware handle the zero-length-packet handshake; IN endpoints only. When off, firmware handles it.

fields.name: SIZE
fields.text: Largest packet the endpoint carries. Codes 0x4 to 0x7 apply to isochronous endpoints only.

fields.name: MULTI_PACKET_SIZE
fields.text: 14-bit count for multi-packet transfers. IN: total bytes sent, written as zero when a new transfer is set up. OUT: total size of the whole transfer, a multiple of the maximum packet size.

fields.name: BYTE_COUNT
fields.text: 14-bit byte count. IN: bytes to send in the next IN transaction. OUT or SETUP: bytes received in the last OUT or SETUP transaction.

registers.name: EXTREG
registers.title: Extended Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xxxxxxxx.

fields.name: VARIABLE
fields.text: VARIABLE field of the last extended token received, updated when the USB has ACKed an LPM transaction. For LPM it splits as VARIABLE[3:0] bLinkState, [7:4] BESL, [8] bRemoteWake, [10:9] reserved, as defined in the USB 2.0 Link Power Management addendum.

fields.name: SUBPID
fields.text: SUBPID field of the last extended token received, updated when the USB has ACKed an LPM transaction.

registers.title: Device Status Bank
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xxxxxxxx.

fields.name: ERROFLOW
fields.text: Set when an error flow is seen on a transfer to or from this bank: a NAK sent on OUT, an overrun on isochronous OUT. Not valid for IN. EPSTATUS.TRFAIL0 and TRFAIL1 reflect flow errors.

fields.name: CRCERR
fields.text: Set when an isochronous OUT bank receives data with a CRC error.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Chooses whether the ADC keeps running in standby sleep mode.

values.text: ADC keeps working in standby sleep.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the ADC on or off; the written value reads back at once while STATUS.SYNCBUSY is set, and SYNCBUSY clears when the change has taken effect after synchronization.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every ADC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disables the ADC; it overrides any other write in the same operation, and both SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY clear once the synchronized reset is done. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: REFCOMP
fields.text: Turns on offset compensation of the reference buffer, which raises gain-stage accuracy but lowers input impedance and lengthens reference start-up.

fields.name: REFSEL
fields.text: Picks the ADC reference: 0x0 INT1V, the 1.0 V internal reference; 0x1 INTVCC0, VDDANA/1.48; 0x2 INTVCC1, VDDANA/2, only when VDDANA is above 2.0 V; 0x3 VREFA and 0x4 VREFB, external references; 0x5-0xF reserved.

values.name: INTVCC1
values.text: VDDANA/2, for VDDANA above 2.0 V only.

fields.name: ADJRES
fields.text: Sets the division coefficient, in steps of 2^n.

fields.name: SAMPLENUM
fields.text: How many samples are summed into RESULT: code n from 0x0 to 0xA sums 2^n samples (1 to 1024); 0xB-0xF reserved. CTRLB.RESSEL has to be changed when the result grows wider.

fields.name: SAMPLEN
fields.text: Sampling time in half CLK_ADC cycles, so it scales with the prescaler, and it sets the ADC input impedance: sampling time = (SAMPLEN + 1) x CLK_ADC/2.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Divides the peripheral clock to make the ADC clock: code n from 0x0 to 0x7 divides by 2^(n+2), DIV4 up to DIV512. Writable only with the ADC disabled.

fields.name: RESSEL
fields.text: Result resolution: 0x0 12-bit; 0x1 16-bit, for averaging output; 0x2 10-bit; 0x3 8-bit. Writable only with the ADC disabled.

fields.name: CORREN
fields.text: Enables gain and offset correction of the result from GAINCAL and OFFSETCAL; conversion takes extra cycles set by the offset correction value. Changeable only with the ADC disabled.

values.text: RESULT is corrected for gain and offset.

fields.name: FREERUN
fields.text: Selects free-running conversion. Changeable only with the ADC disabled.

values.text: Free running: each finished conversion starts the next.

fields.name: LEFTADJ
fields.text: Places the result at the top of RESULT instead of the bottom (0, the default, right-adjusts). Changeable only with the ADC disabled.

values.text: Result left-adjusted in RESULT, high byte of the 12-bit result in the upper byte.

fields.name: DIFFMODE
fields.text: Selects differential conversion of MUXPOS against MUXNEG. Changeable only with the ADC disabled.

values.text: Differential: MUXPOS minus MUXNEG is converted.

fields.name: WINMODE
fields.text: Window monitor mode: 0x0 off (default); 0x1 RESULT > WINLT; 0x2 RESULT < WINUT; 0x3 WINLT < RESULT < WINUT; 0x4 RESULT outside WINLT..WINUT; 0x5-0x7 reserved.

values.name: MODE3
values.text: Mode 3: RESULT between WINLT and WINUT.

values.name: MODE4
values.text: Mode 4: RESULT not between WINLT and WINUT.

fields.name: START
fields.text: Writing 1 starts a conversion; hardware clears it once the conversion begins. Writing 1 while already set, or writing 0, does nothing.

fields.name: FLUSH
fields.text: Writing 1 flushes the ADC pipeline: the ADC clock restarts on the next peripheral clock edge and conversions under way are dropped; the bit reads 0 until the flush has finished, after which the ADC picks up where it was, starting a new conversion if one was pending. Writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Pipeline flushed, conversions in progress lost.

fields.name: GAIN
fields.text: Gain of the ADC gain stage: 0x0 1x; 0x1 2x; 0x2 4x; 0x3 8x; 0x4 16x; 0x5-0xE reserved; 0xF 1/2x.

fields.name: INPUTOFFSET
fields.text: Offset added to MUXPOS for the input actually converted, used by pin scan (active when INPUTSCAN is not 0); nonzero makes the first conversion use MUXPOS + INPUTOFFSET, zero makes it use MUXPOS, and it increments by one after each conversion.

fields.name: INPUTSCAN
fields.text: Number of inputs in the pin scan, minus one; the scan covers MUXPOS + INPUTOFFSET up to MUXPOS + INPUTOFFSET + INPUTSCAN and must stay within the inputs the device has.

fields.name: MUXNEG
fields.text: Selects the negative ADC input.

fields.name: MUXPOS
fields.text: Selects the positive ADC input; choosing the bandgap or temperature sensor needs a matching SAMPCTRL.SAMPLEN.

fields.name: WINMONEO
fields.text: Enables the event output fired when the window monitor detects a match.

fields.name: RESRDYEO
fields.text: Enables the event output fired when a conversion result is ready.

fields.name: SYNCEI
fields.text: Makes an incoming event flush the ADC and start a new conversion.

values.text: Events do not flush or start a conversion.
Any incoming event flushes and starts a conversion.

fields.name: STARTEI
fields.text: Makes an incoming event start a new conversion.

values.text: Events do not start a conversion.
